text: 493mb still feels massive for what the actual scope of what the game data is to be honest. so what is causing so much bloat ?
resolution: Answered 'what is causing so much bloat?' with verified numbers, not hand-waving. The 70MB game-file / 490MB bake peak is NOT real game data: the authored city (buildings, roads, props) is only 6,872 instances = 0.4MB (0.6%). 99.4% — 1,050,792 instances, 56MB — is FOLIAGE (705k grass + 200k palm fronds + 132k bush + 8k trunks + 3k flowers) baked as explicit 56-byte per-blade transform rows. Every blade is a pure deterministic formula: populateFoliage hashes (cell, blade-index, seed) to derive position/yaw/height/width/color, and the only real inputs (which cells are grass) are already in the file as painted floor chunks. So 56MB is the expanded PRODUCT of a formula whose factors are a few KB — the GUIDING_LIGHT 'store the recipe not the dense form' anti-pattern. Confirmed the Zig loader consumes baked rows (has the GrassBlade geometry but reads per-blade placement from the instance buffer; no regeneration). Recommended fix #1 (GL-correct): port populateFoliage into world_loader.zig so it expands blades from the recipe at load time → file 70MB→~14MB, peak→~150MB. Secondary cheap win #2: b.inst is a boxed number[] (105MB) duplicating a 52MB Float32Array; accumulate into a typed array → ~150MB off bake peak (file unchanged). Awaiting user go-ahead before touching the Zig render path.
